title: Set up a premolar bitewing on a dental training head
instruction: Set up a bitewing of the patient's right premolars on the training head: put the holder's plate behind the right premolars, its front edge at the canine and its tab on the lower premolars, close the jaw onto the tab, and let go.
context: Dental assistants (O*NET 31-9091, 388,600 US workers: 'Expose dental diagnostic x-rays') and hygienists (29-1292, 225,300) take bitewings at routine check-ups, several sets a day. The skill is placing the receptor: a 41 x 31 mm plate set at an exact pose inside a true-size mouth, mostly out of sight, behind the premolars, parallel to them, its front edge at the canine; misplaced, the image overlaps or misses teeth and is retaken. Bitewing placement is taught and checked on phantom heads, the instructor or student closing the mandible; the scored skill, the plate placed and kept undisturbed through closure, is the one used on patients, who bite while the operator holds the holder still. With a ring-aiming holder the head may be reclined, as on a dental chair: the cone follows the ring.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), heights above the bench. (1) Dental training head, ANNWAH mouth simulator phantom head, fix-on-table (Amazon B09NB9FSYQ, about $115-160): silicone face mask on a metal head form, 28-tooth resin adult typodont in aluminium jaws, lower jaw on a hinged articulator; no tongue. Clamped to the bench, post ball joint 3 cm up at x 37.5, y 0; facing the robot, reclined 25 deg chin-up; head spans x 29.8-51.4, y -9.1 to 9.1, top at x 42, height 30.6. Jaw hinge axis along y at x 40.9, height 15.8, its hinge (or locking) screw set so the jaw stays at any opening: about 5 N lifting under the chin moves it, and it stays open at its stop and shut on the tab when let go; starts open 30 deg, 48 mm between the incisal edges. Mask mouth opening 52 mm wide; lower incisal edges (jaw shut) at x 31.5, height 16.8. The patient's right is the robot's left (+y). (2) Bitewing holder, assembled, 16 g: Rinn XCP-ORA One Ring & Arm (REF 550771), red XCP bitewing bite block, size 2 phosphor plate (31 x 41 mm) in its barrier envelope; ring 72 mm across, 75 mm out from the plate on the beam axis; the arm's straight leg runs on along the beam axis 45 mm past the ring. It lies plate down, tipped 20 deg onto the plate's long edge, plate centre at x 26.3, y 26.7, height 1.7; the plate's long edge points toward the robot, 9 deg to the robot's right of straight back; the ring is above the plate and the arm's leg sticks out toward the robot, its end at x 15.6, y 24.9, height 10.9. (3) White plastic tray 20 x 13 x 0.8 cm centred x 24.5, y 26.2. Seeds 1 and 2 move tray and holder 1 and 2 cm further in +x. Nothing else on the bench; the scene's lamp only lights the mouth for the camera and is not part of the trial.
scoring: Plate pose in the lower jaw's frame against the target: tab underside on the lower right premolar cusps (plate centre 1.5 mm above the biting plane), plate parallel to their lingual faces 7 mm lingual, front edge level with the canine's distal half. u along the row, v vertical, d plate face to the premolars' lingual faces, h horizontal angulation, t tilt from upright. At the end: 1.0 |u| <= 4 mm, |v| <= 3 mm, d 2-12 mm, h and t <= 10 deg, the jaw closed on the tab (incisal gap 6 mm or less; the tab stops it at about 4 mm), both grippers 3 cm or more from the holder, holder still for the last 1 s (per 50 ms step its plate centre and arm end each move under 1 mm and it turns under 0.5 deg). 0.75 the same within 8 mm, 6 mm, 0-16 mm, 20 deg. 0.5 within the 1.0 band but the jaw open or the holder still held. 0.25 tab resting on the lower right premolars or first molar (within 12 mm along the row, 6 mm vertically, upright within 20 deg). 0 otherwise, including nothing done or the left side; and 0 for the rest of the run if a gripper's fingertip passes the front of the lips into the mouth opening. Real trial: the arm is rigid, so the ring stands for the plate. Calibrate once by placing the holder at the target by hand; a phone on a clamp tripod (e.g. Joby GripTight) clamped at a marked spot on the bench edge, on the beam axis 30 cm out, photographs the ring over an overlay of its calibrated outline with 3/4/6/8 mm circles (no parallax across the axis); protractor and square on base marks give h and t; ring-face distance to a block on the axis gives d; ruler for the incisal gap; a pen line at the slot edge on the plate envelope, checked after opening the jaw, shows the plate stayed in its slot; release, stillness and fingers past the front of the lips from video.
reset_notes: Open the jaw to its 30 degree stop, lay the assembled holder on the tray as in the screenshot (plate down, ring up). Check the hinge still holds the jaw open and shut.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX. Typodont crowns, gums, palate and mask are rigid convex shapes at true size built from the head's and a standard adult typodont's measurements (not scans), the mask is drawn smooth, with colliders for lips, inner cheeks and chin; silicone lips and cheeks are rigid at their stretched size. No tongue, as on the real head. The jaw hinge has static and moving friction (0.45 / 0.38 N m). No X-ray is simulated: the score reads the plate's pose, as the ring calibration does for real.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0. The left arm (left of the video) hovered over the holder on the tray from 10 s to the end, its fingers within 4 mm of it at 70 s, but never lifted it; the right arm stayed near its base; the jaw stayed open. Scripted demo: 1.0.
